root_idea.summary: The root centers on sufficiency: freedom from want, having enough, wealth, and the ability of something to suffice or avail. A separate lexical branch concerns voice, singing, and song.
root_idea.development: The sufficiency branch extends from being free of need to contentment, material wealth, causing someone to be sufficiently provided for, and dwelling contentedly in a place. The root also has an independent voice-and-song branch.

senses.definition: To be or become free from want; to be sufficiently provided for or prosperous.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive use describing a state of sufficiency or prosperity.

senses.definition: To dwell or abide in a place, living there as though content and sufficiently provided for by it.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a place or dwelling; the Quranic expression means that the people had dwelt there.

senses.definition: To avail, enrich, or render sufficient.
senses.usage_conditions: This transitive Quranic usage is represented in the supplied QAC group alongside the intransitive Form I occurrences; it overlaps lexically with the causative use of أَغْنَى.

senses.definition: To enrich, make free from want, or provide with sufficient means.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative use: the subject makes another sufficiently provided for or free from need.

senses.definition: To suffice, avail, stand in the stead of, or spare someone from a thing; with عَنْ, to protect or ward off from it.
senses.usage_conditions: Frequently used in the construction أَغْنَى عَنْهُ; the Quranic contexts include possessions, children, intercession, and other things that fail to avail or avert harm.

senses.definition: To become free from need, do without, or regard oneself as free from need.
senses.usage_conditions: The use may describe actual independence from need or a person's assumption that he has no need of others.
In the Quran, this absolute freedom from every need is properly attributed to God.

senses.definition: Sufficient in oneself, having few wants, or contentedly independent of others.
senses.usage_conditions: A human or other created being may be described as غَنِيّ in the relative sense of having little need or being inwardly self-sufficient.

senses.definition: Rich or possessing substantial property and resources.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of people in relation to their material means; the plural أَغْنِيَاءُ means the rich or wealthy.

senses.definition: One who suffices, avails, or wards off harm.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural مُغْنُونَ refers to those who cannot avail or avert the consequence in question.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To marry or take a wife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Classical Arabic use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain or continue constant, including remaining constant in affection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension distinct from dwelling in a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be, exist, or have been in existence; in certain expressions, to perish or pass away as though one had not existed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Classical usage equivalent in context to كَانَ; it may describe something that has come to nothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To meet or encounter; in a negative expression, not to have met or found someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and lexically disputed usage reported in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sing, chant, trill, or prolong and sweetly modulate the voice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used of singing or chanting poetry and, in a reported expression, of reciting the Quran with a plaintive or gentle voice; a pigeon may also be said to utter its cry in this way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat a person or subject in sung or poetic performance, including amorous mention, praise, or satire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction with بِ may refer to amatory poetry, eulogy, or satire, often with singing or chanting implied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be in no need of another person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III usage related to غَنِيَ عَنْهُ and اِسْتَغْنَى عَنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak or talk to a child in a pleasing manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, tentatively reported Form III usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: How free from want, or how rich, someone is!
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anomalous or non-regular exclamatory construction reported for this verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become free from want of one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction expressing mutual independence or lack of need.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or beg God to make one free from want or rich.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive devotional construction addressed to God, distinct from the ordinary intransitive Form X use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A suitable, fitting, or appropriate place or circumstance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression of a place being suitable for someone, literally suggesting freedom from want there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Freedom from need, competence, or sufficiency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or simple substantive; it can denote having enough to sustain oneself or being free from dependence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Profit, utility, or avail; something sufficient or useful in place of another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or thing that is profitable, useful, or able to stand in another's stead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sufficiency, competence, or freedom from want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal form related to غِنًى but lexically distinct in the supplied entries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ability, strength, or capacity to set something up, bear it, carry it, or raise it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression that a person lacks the capacity to undertake or support something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Singing, chanting, vocal music, a song, or poetry performed with modulation of the voice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote the act or manner of singing, a musical performance, a tune, or a sung composition; the exact forms and plurals vary by usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A singer; by extension, a female singer or songstress in the related feminine form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The explanation connects the term with producing a nasal or resonant quality in the voice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who is satisfied with or sufficed by her husband, beauty, or circumstances and therefore has no need of adornment or another man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied evidence records several Classical explanations, including being content with one's husband, being beautiful without ornament, or being youthful and chaste; these are lexical explanations rather than a single obligatory restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The goods, ornaments, or paraphernalia of brides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare plural noun for bridal possessions; the singular is not supplied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of habitation or abode, especially a place in which people lived or by which they were once provided and satisfied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer specifically to an inhabited or formerly inhabited dwelling, or more generally to a place of abode.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who satisfies or contents whom He wills of His servants; a divine name or epithet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical theological specialization of the active participle and is not assigned as a separate Quranic sense of مُغْنُونَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who satisfies or contents her husband so that he has no need to look at another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine active-participial specialization.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Free from want, sufficiency, and contentment are represented.
Dwelling in a place, including the cited Quranic expression.
Living is covered by the Quranic dwelling sense.
Cooing or vocalizing is covered by the vocalization branch.
Amatory, laudatory, and satirical poetic use.
Reported pleasing speech to a child.
Sufficing, availing, and averting in Quranic constructions.
Pointer-only reference to the intransitive use.
Capacity to bear or undertake something.
Inflectional cross-reference identifying a verbal noun.
Poetry used as the act of singing or chanting.
Freedom from want, relative sufficiency, and wealth.
Active participle meaning one who suffices.

cautions: The supplied QAC Form I group contains both أَغْنَىٰ-like surfaces and يَغْنَ surfaces while being labeled Form I; the public citation form follows the supplied Form I morphology, and the transitive usage is explicitly flagged as overlapping the Form IV causative.
The Form I and Form IV QAC groupings should not be read as eliminating the lexical overlap between the supplied أَغْنَىٰ occurrences and the causative meaning attested in the lexical evidence.
The rare Classical uses for meeting, speaking pleasingly to a child, bride goods, and exclamatory أَغْنَى are retained because they are explicitly reported, but they are not ordinary Quranic senses.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The supplied QAC Form I morphology groups homographic or formally mixed occurrences, so the division between its intransitive prosperity/dwelling uses and its transitive avail/enrich uses is retained with an explicit overlap caution rather than silently reassigning occurrences.
